newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians demonstrate in Gaza - radio.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians demonstrate in Gaza - radio.

text.p: Thousands of Arabs demonstrated in Khan Younis in the Gaza Strip self-rule enclave on Friday, the first Palestinian protest in Gaza or the West Bank since fierce Arab-Israeli clashes a day earlier, Israel Army Radio said.
It said some Palestinians in the crowd fired into the air but so far the protest was confined to the Palestinian town and there was no contact with Israelis.

Israel blamed the Palestinian Authority on Friday for two days of gun battles sparked by Israel's opening on Tuesday of an archaeological tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem. More than 50 people have been killed.

"The government of Israel is demanding of the Palestinian Authority to cease the incitement and to restrain the violent activity in its territory against Israeli civilians and Israeli army soldiers," Israel's security cabinet said in a statement issued after seven hours of emergency talks late on Thursday.
A senior Israeli official said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu urgently wanted a meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to stop the bloodshed.

But PLO officials said Arafat would have little success in quelling the violence unless assured that Netanyahu would commit himself at the meeting to implementing the peace deals of the government he defeated in elections last May.
